project.name: Human Hum
project.description: Personal music scrobbling platform — records listening history and surfaces insights. Monorepo with Next.js 16, Drizzle ORM, Neon Postgres.

nodes.name: schema.ts
nodes.summary: Star schema definition with dimension tables (artists, albums, tracks) and a fact table (scrobbles) in a 'listen' Postgres schema, using Drizzle ORM.

nodes.name: shared.ts
nodes.summary: Defines the 'listen' pgSchema and reusable timestamp column mixins (createdAt, updatedAt, deletedAt) for Drizzle table definitions.

nodes.name: index.ts
nodes.summary: DB client factory using Neon serverless driver with HMR-safe global singleton pattern. Exports createDb, db instance, schema, and Database type.

nodes.name: ingestion.ts
nodes.summary: Implements recordListen, the core entity-resolution pipeline that idempotently resolves artist/album/track dimensions and inserts scrobble facts with race-condition safety.

nodes.name: ingestion.test.ts
nodes.summary: Integration tests for recordListen covering new scrobbles, duplicate detection, optional albums, missing MBIDs, and entity reuse across tracks.

nodes.name: test-utils.ts
nodes.summary: Shared PGlite test setup that creates an in-memory Postgres instance with the full listen schema DDL for integration testing.

nodes.name: createDb
nodes.summary: Creates a Drizzle ORM database instance from a Neon serverless connection URL.

nodes.name: resolveEntity
nodes.summary: Select-Insert-Reselect pattern for race-condition-safe idempotent entity resolution. Returns the entity ID whether it existed or was just created.

nodes.name: recordListen
nodes.summary: Core ingestion function that resolves artist, album, and track entities then inserts or finds a scrobble fact row, returning all resolved IDs and a wasNew flag.

nodes.name: setupTestDb
nodes.summary: Creates an in-memory PGlite instance, applies the full listen schema DDL, and returns a Drizzle database handle for integration tests.

nodes.name: types.ts
nodes.summary: Shared TypeScript types for the query layer, including ScrobbleFilter, pagination params, ranking types, detail types, time-series buckets, and listening clock slots.

nodes.name: filter.ts
nodes.summary: Builds Drizzle ORM WHERE clause conditions from a ScrobbleFilter object. Provides buildFilterConditions for scrobble-level columns and addArtistCondition for joined artist filtering.

nodes.name: scrobbles.ts
nodes.summary: Scrobble listing and detail queries with offset and cursor-based pagination, joining tracks/artists/albums tables.

nodes.name: artists.ts
nodes.summary: Artist ranking and detail queries: getArtistRankings returns top-N artists by play count, getArtistDetail returns artist info with top tracks and albums.

nodes.name: albums.ts
nodes.summary: Album detail query returning album info, artist name, play count, and track listing with per-track play counts.

nodes.name: stats.ts
nodes.summary: Aggregate statistics query returning total scrobbles, date range, and unique counts for artists, tracks, and albums.

nodes.name: time-series.ts
nodes.summary: Time-based analytics queries: getTimeSeries buckets scrobbles by day/week/month/year using date_trunc, getListeningClock counts scrobbles per hour of day.

nodes.name: index.ts
nodes.summary: Barrel file re-exporting all query functions and types from the queries submodules.

nodes.name: queries.test.ts
nodes.summary: Integration tests for all query functions using PGlite, seeding 6 scrobbles across 3 artists and verifying pagination, filtering, rankings, details, time series, and listening clock.

nodes.name: buildFilterConditions
nodes.summary: Converts a ScrobbleFilter into an array of Drizzle SQL conditions for time range, source, trackId, and albumId.

nodes.name: getScrobbles
nodes.summary: Returns paginated scrobble rows with total count, supporting offset pagination, cursor-based pagination, time range, source, and artist filters.

nodes.name: getScrobbleById
nodes.summary: Fetches a single scrobble by ID with full track/artist/album info plus track and artist play counts.

nodes.name: getArtistRankings
nodes.summary: Returns top-N artists ranked by play count, with optional ScrobbleFilter for time range and source filtering.

nodes.name: getArtistDetail
nodes.summary: Returns detailed artist info including total play count, top 10 tracks, and top 10 albums for a given artist ID.

nodes.name: getAlbumDetail
nodes.summary: Returns album info with artist name, total play count, and track listing with per-track play counts.

nodes.name: getStats
nodes.summary: Returns aggregate scrobble statistics: total count, earliest/latest dates, and unique artist/track/album counts.

nodes.name: getTimeSeries
nodes.summary: Buckets scrobbles into time periods (day/week/month/year) using SQL date_trunc, returning period-count pairs.

nodes.name: getListeningClock
nodes.summary: Counts scrobbles per hour of day (0-23), filling missing hours with zero counts to always return 24 slots.

nodes.name: source-fetcher.ts
nodes.summary: Defines the SourceFetcher interface for source-agnostic scrobble fetching and the importScrobbles orchestration function that handles incremental sync, full backfill, backfill resume, pagination, progress reporting, and completeness checking.

nodes.name: lastfm.ts
nodes.summary: LastFM-specific implementation of SourceFetcher. Contains LastfmFetcher class that calls the Last.fm API (user.getRecentTracks, user.getInfo) with retry/backoff logic, and re-exports orchestration types for convenience.

nodes.name: source-fetcher.test.ts
nodes.summary: Integration tests for importScrobbles orchestration using a FakeFetcher and PGlite in-memory DB. Covers single-page import, pagination, deduplication, incremental sync from-detection, backfill resume to-detection, progress callbacks, and completeness checking.

nodes.name: lastfm.ts (CLI)
nodes.summary: CLI entry point for LastFM scrobble import. Reads env vars (LASTFM_API_KEY, LASTFM_USER, DATABASE_URL), parses --backfill flag, creates LastfmFetcher and db, then calls importScrobbles with progress logging.

nodes.name: LastfmFetcher
nodes.summary: Implements SourceFetcher for Last.fm. Fetches scrobble pages via user.getRecentTracks API (with retry/backoff) and remote play count via user.getInfo. Transforms LastFM track JSON into ListenInput objects, skipping now-playing entries.

nodes.name: importScrobbles
nodes.summary: Source-agnostic scrobble import orchestrator. Handles three modes: incremental sync (auto-detects from=latest-1s), full backfill (all pages at 200/page), and backfill resume (sets to=earliest+1s). Paginates through fetcher, records each listen via recordListen, reports progress, and optionally checks completeness.

nodes.name: LastfmFetcher.fetchPage
nodes.summary: Fetches a single page of recent tracks from Last.fm API. Builds URL with pagination/date params, calls fetchWithRetry, then transforms track JSON into ListenInput array, skipping now-playing entries without timestamps.

nodes.name: LastfmFetcher.getRemotePlaycount
nodes.summary: Calls Last.fm user.getInfo API to retrieve total play count for completeness verification after backfill.

nodes.name: fetchWithRetry
nodes.summary: Fetches a URL with exponential backoff retry logic (up to 5 retries). Handles both network errors and HTTP 429 rate-limit responses with increasing delay (200ms * 2^attempt).

tour.title: Data Model: The Star Schema Foundation
tour.description: Everything in Human Hum rests on a star schema. shared.ts defines the 'listen' Postgres schema namespace and reusable timestamp mixins, while schema.ts declares three dimension tables (artists, albums, tracks) and one fact table (scrobbles). Each scrobble references a track, which references an artist and optionally an album. This dimension/fact pattern means you can slice listening data by any combination of artist, album, track, or time period without denormalizing.

tour.title: Entity Resolution: From Raw Listen to Normalized Entities
tour.description: When a scrobble arrives, it is just a bag of strings (artist name, track title, album name). ingestion.ts turns this into proper database entities. The resolveEntity function uses a select-insert-refetch pattern that is safe against race conditions: it tries to find an existing row, inserts if missing, and re-selects if the insert hits a unique constraint. recordListen orchestrates this for artist, album, and track in sequence, then inserts the scrobble fact row.

tour.title: SourceFetcher Interface: The Import Pipeline Port
tour.description: source-fetcher.ts defines the SourceFetcher interface, the abstraction that decouples import orchestration from any specific music service. A SourceFetcher must implement fetchPage (paginated scrobble retrieval) and getRemotePlaycount (total count for completeness checks). The importScrobbles function is the orchestrator that handles three modes: incremental sync, full backfill, and backfill resume, all by delegating page fetches to the SourceFetcher and entity resolution to recordListen.

tour.title: LastFM Fetcher: Concrete API Integration
tour.description: LastfmFetcher is the concrete SourceFetcher implementation for Last.fm. It calls user.getRecentTracks to fetch scrobble pages and user.getInfo for the remote play count. The fetchWithRetry helper adds resilience with exponential backoff (up to 5 retries, handling HTTP 429 rate limits). The fetcher transforms Last.fm's JSON track format into the ListenInput shape expected by recordListen, skipping now-playing entries that lack timestamps.

tour.title: CLI Entry Point: Wiring Environment to Pipeline
tour.description: The import CLI at apps/import/src/lastfm.ts is intentionally thin. It reads environment variables (LASTFM_API_KEY, LASTFM_USER, DATABASE_URL), parses a --backfill flag, creates a LastfmFetcher and database connection, then hands everything to importScrobbles with a progress-logging callback. This separation keeps all logic in the library while the CLI is just a wiring layer.

tour.title: Query Layer Foundation: Filters and WHERE Clauses
tour.description: The query layer starts with two files that every query depends on. types.ts defines the ScrobbleFilter type (time range, source, artist, track, album constraints) plus pagination, ranking, and time-series result shapes. filter.ts provides buildFilterConditions, which converts a ScrobbleFilter into an array of Drizzle SQL conditions. This shared foundation means every query function accepts the same filter interface and produces consistent WHERE clauses.

tour.title: Query Functions: Domain-Specific Data Access
tour.description: Each query module exposes named functions for a specific domain. getScrobbles handles paginated listing with both offset and cursor modes. getArtistRankings and getArtistDetail power the artist views. getAlbumDetail returns track listings with per-track play counts. getStats computes aggregate dashboard numbers. getTimeSeries and getListeningClock bucket scrobbles by time period and hour-of-day respectively. Each function hides Drizzle join complexity behind a clean interface.

tour.title: DB Client: Factory and Singleton
tour.description: index.ts ties the database layer together. createDb is a factory function that takes a Neon connection URL and returns a Drizzle ORM instance. For the web app running in HMR, a global singleton pattern ensures only one connection pool exists across hot reloads. The file also re-exports the schema and all query functions, so consumers import everything from @workspace/db.

tour.title: App Shell: Layout, Sidebar, and Header
tour.description: The web app visual frame is assembled in layout.tsx, which wraps all pages with ThemeProvider, TooltipProvider, and SidebarProvider, then renders AppSidebar and AppHeader around the page content. AppSidebar provides navigation links (Scrobbles, Artists, Albums, Stats) with active-state highlighting. AppHeader renders breadcrumbs derived from the current pathname. Together they create the consistent chrome users see on every page.

tour.title: Scrobbles Page: Server-Rendered Listing
tour.description: The scrobbles page is a Next.js Server Component that demonstrates the full read path. ScrobblesPage parses the page search param, calls getScrobbles with offset pagination, and renders results in an HTML table with track, artist, album, and timestamp columns. The getPageNumbers utility computes pagination controls with ellipsis gaps. Every row links to the scrobble detail page. No client JavaScript is needed for the initial render.

tour.title: Scrobble Detail: Single Record Deep Dive
tour.description: The scrobble detail page at /scrobbles/[id] shows the full context of a single listen event. ScrobbleDetailPage extracts the ID from route params, calls getScrobbleById (which joins across all dimension tables and computes play counts), and renders a metadata grid showing track name, artist, album, timestamp, source, plus how many times the track and artist have been played overall. This closes the loop from import to display.

tour.title: Test Infrastructure: PGlite Integration Testing
tour.description: The project uses PGlite, an in-memory Postgres implementation, for integration tests that run without external services. test-utils.ts provides setupTestDb, which creates a PGlite instance and applies the full listen schema DDL. The ingestion and query test files seed realistic data through the same recordListen function used in production, then verify behavior end-to-end. This pattern gives high confidence without Docker or network dependencies.
